newsitem.title: USA: Delaware grand jury indicts teens in baby's death.
newsitem.headline: Delaware grand jury indicts teens in baby's death.

text.p: A Delaware grand jury indicted two 18-year-olds on first degree murder charges Monday in the death of their infant son shortly after his birth in a motel room Nov. 12.

Amy Grossberg and Brian Peterson, who grew up in affluent suburbs of northern New Jersey, were charged with intentionally causing the death of the baby and murder by abuse or neglect. They face a possible death penalty if convicted of intentionally causing the boy's death.
They are to be arraigned this week or next, although it is possible to bypass a court hearing for the process.
Peterson's attorney, Joseph Hurley, said he would seek bail for his client and would seek to show at the bail hearing that authorities lacked the necessary proof to hold Peterson.
The second charge, murder by abuse or neglect, is punishable by life in prison without parole.

Police found the infant's body wrapped in a plastic bag in a dumpster behind the motel in Newark, Del. The state medical examiner reported that the baby had died of "multiple skull fractures, blunt-force head trauma and shaking."

Delaware Attorney General Jane Brady said she would seek the death penalty for Grossberg and Peterson because of the autopsy report and because Delaware law classifies the murder of a child under 14 as a capital offence.

Grossberg has been in the Baylor Correctional Institution in New Castle, Del., since her discharge from Christiana Hospital in Newark where, hours after the baby was born, she was admitted for complications related to the delivery.

Peterson avoided arrest at first by going into seclusion with his mother, Barbara Zuchowski. But on Nov. 14 he turned himself in to the Wilmington office of the FBI. He has been in Gander Hill Prison in Wilmington since then and, like Grossberg, kept isolated from the general prison population.
Grossberg and Peterson had been sweethearts at Ramapo Regional High School in the affluent New York suburb of Franklin Lakes, N.J.. They graduated in June.
Peterson, a freshman at Gettysburg College in Pennsylvania, has been suspended from the institution. Grossberg was a freshman at the University of Delaware in Newark.
